pull.title: feat(os-pane): add a Swarm tab so workflow runs and helper agents have a place to show
pull.body:
Workflow runs and helper agents showed only as a count on the `/os` Overview, so there was no place to see which agents run, in which phase, and for how long. Swarm is now the seventh `/os` tab: one line per workflow run with its phase and agent counts, then one line per agent, cut to fit 20 to 200 columns. The phase comes from the workflow journal, read only when `/os` opens and on a Swarm press.

## Evidence

Proof type: feature

RED: `claude plugin test .claude/plugins/ccv3-mods` (repo root, `TYPES_SRC` set) @ 4de9df29
```text
 1032 pass
 29 fail
Ran 1061 tests across 34 files. [40.55s]  (swarm-tab.test.ts did not load)
```

GREEN: `node scripts/mods/validate-mods.mjs` (repo root, `TYPES_SRC` set) @ 59e926bb
```text
mods OK: validate OK (16 gating hooks, 0 without .catch) | tsc OK (types 2026-10-28) | test 1154 pass 0 fail
```

CLI fix review: f7ce2c2..59e926b clean (`cr-fix.mjs --pr 231`, output `.claude/cache/e2e/2026-10-30-cr-fix-59e926b.txt`). CodeRabbit's one Minor finding (the README said "8 newest runs", the code takes running runs first) is a one-line docs fix in `59e926bb`.

The RED commit holds only tests, so the 29 failures are the Swarm model, the seventh tab and the tab list. A second test-first commit (`cbc907a0`) pins the journal feed and the Swarm press: 12 more tests failed before `6971b5cb`. The review fixes were also test first: 10 failed before `2a37bf1c`.

Live check (`atlas`, a real interactive session through a pseudo-terminal, Sonnet at low effort, two throwaway workflows): the strip shows `7: Swarm`, the footer reads `later: Comms · Resources`, a running workflow shows its phase and one line per agent (label, status, time, and the model badge from 80 columns), and no row is wider than its pane at 40, 80, 110 and 200 columns. 14 captured frames.

Mutation checks: for each new test group a source change was made on a scratch copy and a test failed (the tables are in the artifact files). One mutant survived by design: `TIME_MIN` 24 to 20, because `wrapRows` and `fitRow` both drop the same group.

Artifacts (gitignored, `.claude/cache/e2e/`): `2026-10-30-os-swarm-tab-live.txt`, `2026-10-30-swarm-s1-3-*.txt`, `2026-10-30-swarm-s4-*.txt`, `2026-10-30-swarm-fix-*.txt`, `2026-10-30-swarm-probe-poll.txt`.

## What changed

- `hooks/agentic-os/swarm-tab.ts` (new): the pure Swarm model. A run row with phase and counts, helper rows with mark, label, model badge and time; finished helpers of a workflow fold into `✓ N done`; a tiny pane drops the HELPERS head.
- `hooks/agentic-os/journal-model.ts` (new): reads `journal.jsonl` of a workflow (label and phase per agent) and, once the run has ended, `runId`, `workflowName` and the phase count from the run file. A size cap, an id and path whitelist, redaction and clipping of every string; a missing or unreadable file gives no feed and never blocks the pane.
- `hooks/agentic-os/cells.ts` (new): terminal-cell width, so wide (CJK, emoji) labels never pass the pane. `text.ts` also strips bidi and zero-width characters.
- `os-tabs-model.ts`, `tab-words.ts`, `types/index.d.ts`: the seventh tab (digit 7, after Choices); the footer lists only Comms and Resources as later.
- `index.tsx`: a Swarm press refreshes the agent list and reads the journal; `/os` open reads it once. The pulse and the other tabs never read it.
- `digest.ts`: helper items cut with a bare `…`, no hint to a tab that may hide them.
- `README.md` and the PRD: the tab list, the Swarm rows, the journal read and its caps.

## Review before this PR

One Opus critic: 3 medium and 6 low findings, all fixed test first in `2a37bf1c`: a hint to a tab that may hide the item, a stale phase while helpers run, and width counted in characters rather than cells; also bidi characters, a missing phase-cap test, run ordering and the byte wording.

Known behaviour, not a bug: a running workflow shows `phase 1: One · a workflow`, with no phase total and no name, because the journal holds neither until the run ends. After the run ends and Swarm is pressed again, the row shows `phase 1 of 1: One · <name>`. The pane reads the journal only at `/os` open and on a Swarm press, so the phase is as fresh as the last press. After `/clear` Swarm starts empty (plugin atoms do not survive).

## Scope not included

- The terminal Fleet view of other sessions (next PR: lane board plus the per-session state files).
- Folding finished workflows into one Overview row, and showing failed helpers under WATCH.
- A detail view per run and a key scheme beyond the digits.
- The Plan tab cut of the running task when no step is done (exists on main, noted on the lane).
- `node scripts/mods/e2e-headless.mjs`: it makes real `claude -p` runs with a cost cap. Dave decides on that spend.

_doc: classes: path globs per risk class. Only ** (any number of whole path segments, also zero), * (inside one segment) and ? are special.

A glob that starts with ! is an exclusion for that class (r3 excludes eval fixtures under .claude/skills/**/evals/**). Each path gets the first class that matches it, in this order: r3, infra, steering, docs.
A path that matches no class is normal. The PR class is the highest class of any path. risk:high is never set from paths: a person adds it.
deep_enabled false: steering, infra, high and r3 PRs get review:coderabbit + review:deep-held, not review:deep (spec 4.1, Apex billing D3).
greptile.credits_used_manual: Greptile credits used this period, an integer you edit by hand. null means unknown: the router skips the u1 and u2 steps and the ledger says so.
greptile.u1_used: at or above this count, a review:deep PR gets a warning in the router comment.
greptile.u2_used: at or above this count, only r3 PRs get review:deep. Other deep classes get the held labels. Needs deep_enabled true.

greptile.u3_date: on or after this date, a deep-class PR gets one credit-check line in the router comment, but only while credits_used_manual is null. A known count means the check is done, so no line.
greptile.notify_login: GitHub login named in the u1 and u3 lines. null means nobody is pinged.
budget: CodeRabbit PR reviews per class as [opening, extra after a Major] (pr-review-loop.md 'PR review budget per class'). Read by scripts/github/pr-checkpoint.mjs. A bare number is [n, 0].

checkpoint.critical: path globs of files whose PR gets Greptile too when it is available (pr-checkpoint.mjs rule R3). A PR that touches one never takes the READY carry (review-status.mjs). Extended 2026-10-30 with the files where a fix added a real Major (.claudedocs/2026-10-30-coderabbit-rereview-study.md section 4).
checkpoint.parser: path globs of hand-written lexer and parser guards. Their PR gets one CodeRabbit review and no loop (rule R2). Dave edits this list.

checkpoint.enforce: boolean, read by the pre-pr-gate hook from the checkout the session runs in. true (live since PR D, 2026-10-29): the checkpoint rules (non-draft create, shell gh pr ready, hand review: label, self-confirm, non-literal --repo) deny the command. false (warn mode): the same commands pass and log one warn row to guard-decisions.jsonl. Only a literal true enforces. The stamp rules are enforced in both modes.

coderabbit.reviews_7d_manual: CodeRabbit PR reviews in the last 7 days, an integer Dave sets from the free '@coderabbitai rate limit' reply or the dashboard CSV export. null means unknown and changes no rule. reviews_7d_manual_date: the day Dave read it. A count older than 7 days counts as unknown.
